[untitled BTM module] The genes here sketch late erythroid differentiation and the assembly of the red cell surface. Erythropoiesis matters because it supplies the circulating oxygen carriers, and its transcriptional and membrane components determine both red cell mechanical resilience and the antigens that decide transfusion compatibility.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on stress-activated transcriptional signalling and its supporting membrane and metabolic machinery. Its recognisable core is the kinase TAK1 (MAP3K7) acting upstream of the CREB/ATF family factors ATF1 and ATF2, a route by which cytokine, TGF-beta and stress inputs are converted into changes in gene expression governing inflammation, survival and differentiation; loss of TAK1 signalling causes inflammatory and developmental failure.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the erythroid-megakaryocytic branch of hematopoiesis, the programme by which bone marrow progenitors commit to making red cells and platelets rather than lymphoid or granulocytic fates. Its transcriptional core is a TAL1-GFI1B axis that drives erythroid gene expression while restraining progenitor proliferation; loss of either blocks red cell production, and GFI1B mutation causes a bleeding disorder with malformed platelets.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.

members: [untitled BTM module] Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. Lipid composition and cytoskeletal geometry are managed alongside cargo flow: the inositol phosphatase SYNJ1 dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 to uncoat vesicles after endocytosis, TMEM30A serves as the accessory subunit that allows P4-ATPase flippases to translocate aminophospholipids across bilayers, and the microtubule-severing ATPase SPAST shapes tubules and axonal microtubule arrays.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on membrane lipid organisation and the trafficking and signalling events built on it. Its clearest core is the aminophospholipid flippase machinery: ATP11B, a P4-ATPase, must partner with the accessory subunit TMEM30A (CDC50A) to fold, reach the plasma membrane and translocate phosphatidylserine to the cytosolic leaflet, which keeps this lipid hidden until apoptosis or platelet activation exposes it.
